title: Power Tools
summary: Power tools are extremely hazardous when used improperly. Keep guards on, check cords and grounding, use the right switches, and disconnect tools before servicing.
talking_points: Five basic rules: keep tools in good condition, use the right tool for the job, examine each tool for damage before use, follow the manufacturer's instructions, and use the right PPE.
Never carry a tool by the cord or hose. Never yank the cord or hose to unplug it. Keep cords and hoses away from heat, oil, and sharp edges.
Disconnect tools when not in use, before servicing or cleaning, and when changing blades, bits, or cutters.
Never remove safety guards while a tool is in use. A circular saw with a blade over 2 inches needs an upper guard and a lower guard that returns to cover the teeth automatically.
Secure your work with clamps or a vise so both hands are free. Do not hold a finger on the switch while carrying a plugged-in tool.

Electric tools need a three-wire cord plugged into a grounded receptacle, double insulation, or a low-voltage isolation transformer. Never remove the third prong. On construction sites, use GFCIs or an assured equipment grounding conductor program.
Inspect and ring-test an abrasive wheel before mounting it. Never stand in the plane of rotation as the wheel comes up to speed. Always use eye or face protection.
Remove damaged portable electric tools from use and tag them "Do Not Use." Avoid loose clothing, ties, and jewelry that can catch in moving parts.
site_hazards_to_check: Damaged cords or plugs, or a removed third prong
Temporary power without GFCI or an assured equipment grounding conductor program
Abrasive wheels that sound cracked or dead when tapped
Electric tools used in damp or wet locations they are not approved for, or cords creating a trip hazard
Damaged tools still in use with no "Do Not Use" tag
discussion_questions: What do you check on a power tool before you plug it in?
